title: When the Old Comes Calling
author: Tshiamo Ramokgadi
body:
The Cost of the Call: When the Old Life Comes Calling

*“I know, Lord, that our lives are not our own; it is not for man to direct his steps.”*
— Jeremiah 10:23

*“You arenot your own; you were bought at a price.”*
— 1 Corinthians 6:19–20

“Sorry batswadi baka, nna ke nyaka strata!

I shouted at the top of my lungs. Bottles flying all over the place. Sparkles left, right and centre. Disco lights flashing. Music playing. And there I was, completely immersed in the atmosphere. And somewhere in the middle of all of it, I had a moment where I thought:

How did Iget here?

Earlier that day, a friend had invited me to this place, and I said no.

I knew better.

Knowing what I know now, knowing who I am in Christ and what He has brought me out of, I didn't think that environment was something that resonated with where I was in my walk with God, but life has a way of testing you. A few minutes before my boy came to fetch me, I received a very nasty phone call. It caught me completely off guard and left me shaken.

And in that moment, I wanted relief.

I wanted comfort.

I wanted something to take my mind off what I had just experienced and this is where I realised something about myself: when I am hurting, I can either anchor myself in Christ or look for something else to numb the discomfort. That day, my faith was rocky.

So when my boy presented me with the same opportunity a few hours later, I budged. We told ourselves we were just going to watch the rugby and come back.

Why was Iying to myself? A pizza here. A few conversations there. Music playing. People laughing. And slowly, I forgot what I had been feeling.

But the truth is, I hadn't dealt with it.

I had simply found another place to put it.

Instead of taking my pain to Christ, I sought my own form of comfort and as the night progressed, the disco lights became dimmer, the music became louder, and I found myself entranced by the very atmosphere I had once walked away from in pursuit of God .The beats, The environment, The familiarity and suddenly I realised something uncomfortable:

I was becoming comfortable with something God had delivered me from. I think sometimes we forget just how much God has done for us. We remember that He saved us, but we forget what He saved us from. We celebrate the new life but sometimes become nostalgic about the old one.

And that's dangerous.

Because when God begins to pull you out of something, He doesn't simply want to change your location. He wants to transform your desires, your thinking, your habits and ultimately your allegiance. There are things God has removed from my life that I cannot afford to romanticise again. There are environments I cannot afford to become comfortable in again. There are versions of myself that I cannot afford to resurrect simply because I am having a bad day.

Because being saved means something.

Paul writes:

*“You are not your own; you were bought at a price.”*

Thats entence hits differently when you actually sit with it.

I am not my own.

My life belongs to Christ. Not only when things are going well. Not only when I feel spiritually strong. Not only when I am in church, worshipping, praying and reading my Bible. He is Lord in the uncomfortable moments too. He is Lord when I'm angry. He is Lord when I'm disappointed. He is Lord when I receive a phone call that completely throws me off. He is Lord when I am tempted to seek comfort somewhere else and that is where the meaning of Kyrios becomes so powerful.

When the New Testament declares that *Jesus is Lord*, it isn't merely giving Him a respectable title. Kyrios carries the idea of lordship, authority and ownership.

When I said yes to Jesus, I wasn't simply asking Him to save me from hell. I was surrendering the right to govern my life independently of Him. **Jesus is Lord.**

Which means He gets to speak into every part of my life. Where I go. Who I spend time with. What I consume. What I pursue. What I run to when I am hurting and even what I do when nobody is watching.

**The Old Life Will Sometimes Call Your Name**

I think one of the hardest parts of walking with God is realising that being delivered doesn't mean you will never be tempted again. The Israelites experienced this. God brought them out of Egypt, yet they eventually found themselves looking back toward the very things they had been delivered from. And if I'm honest, I've seen this tendency in myself too.

You can leave something physically and still have to learn how to leave it mentally.

You can be delivered from something and still have moments where the old thing looks attractive.

You can know better and still make a bad decision.

That doesn't mean God hasn't changed you.

It means you're still being refined and perhaps that's why Peter tells us to be sober and watchful because the enemy is prowling around looking for someone to devour.

We cannot afford to become careless.

Because sometimes the enemy doesn't need to introduce you to something new.

Sometime she simply reminds you of something old. Grace Doesn't Give Me Permission to Go Back

But here's the beautiful part.

This isn't a message of condemnation.

It's a message of remembrance, because yes, I went somewhere I probably shouldn't have gone. Yes, I allowed my emotions to influence a decision I had already made. Yes, I found comfort somewhere other than Christ. But His grace is still there. I may stumble, but His blood is forever And that distinction matters.

The answer isn't to sit in shame and tell myself I'm a failure. The answer is to recognise where I went wrong, bring it before God, receive His grace and keep walking. Because Jesus didn't save me so that I could spend my life being terrified of falling. He saved me so that I could walk in freedom and freedom means learning what to walk away from.

**So, What's Your Kryptonite?**

I don't know what yours is.

Maybe it's a relationship.

Maybe it's a habit.

Maybe it's a certain environment.

Maybe it's validation.

Maybe it's your old way of dealing with pain.

Maybe it's something that you keep telling yourself you have control over.

Whatever it is, I want to encourage you:

Don't lose sight of what God has brought you out of. Don't romanticise the prison because you've forgotten what freedom feels like. Don't return to Egypt simply because the wilderness became uncomfortable and when you find yourself slipping, don't run away from God in shame.

**Run back to Him.**

The Christian walk isn't about pretending we never struggle.

It's about knowing where to go when we do.

I shared my kryptonite with you because perhaps someone reading this has their own and maybe today is simply a reminder that Jesus is still Lord not just over the good parts of your life, but over all of it. Your weak moments. Your painful moments. Your confusing moments. Your temptations. Your decisions. Your future.

All of it.

Jesus loves you.

And if He has brought you out before, trust Him enough to let Him continue refining you.

Keep walking. Keep surrendering. Keep choosing Him.

And when the old life comes calling remember who you are, remember whose you are, and remember what He saved you from.\
\
**Selah**
